judged_text: The findFirst-then-create/update sequence has no concurrency guard or idempotency key, so two in-flight deliveries of the same webhook both take the create branch. A webhook retried while the first delivery is still in flight (senders retry on timeout and this handler has no dedup) creates duplicate (userId, appId) credential rows; later findFirst returns an arbitrary row, so updates can land on a different credential than the one the app reads, leaving stale keys flapping.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the credential write path is a non-atomic `findFirst` followed by either `credential.update` or `credential.create`. This introduces a race window where concurrent/duplicate webhook deliveries can both observe “no row” and proceed to `create`, unless there is a DB-level unique constraint on `(userId, appId)` (not shown in this diff). Even if such a constraint exists, the handler doesn’t handle a unique-violation retry/resolve. The finding’s specific claim about duplicates and “arbitrary row” depends on schema guarantees not visible here, but the concurrency/idempotency concern is diff-grounded.
